1: Welcome to Boost Sales with AI! Meet Amaka, who sells ready-to-wear outfits in Yaba, Lagos, and Chidi, who looks after her orders.
AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude are writing and thinking assistants, ready to help them sell.
AI is very good at drafting text, summing things up, brainstorming new ideas, and even playing the role of a customer.
But AI does not know your prices, your stock, or your customers.
Unless you tell it. So keep a short note of your business facts, and paste it in when you ask for help.
Here is the golden rule. A vague request gets a vague answer.
A good prompt says who you are,
and the format you want it in.
Now the answer fits your business, and it's ready to post.
Let's get set up. Create free accounts on ChatGPT and Claude.
Install their phone apps, so AI sits right next to WhatsApp, wherever you are.
Then write your business facts note: prices, delivery areas, payment and returns, ready to paste into any prompt.
Two safety rules. First, AI can get facts and numbers wrong, so always check them before you post.
Second, never paste private details, like card numbers or full addresses. Keep your customers safe.
Before the next lesson, create your accounts and install the apps.
Write your business facts note, and try one prompt with full context.
In lesson two, we will use AI to get to know your customer. See you there!
2: Welcome back! Meet Amaka. She sells ready-to-wear outfits from her boutique in Yaba, Lagos. And this is Chidi, who answers her WhatsApp and Instagram orders.
In lesson one, you learned the golden rule: give AI context.
Today, Amaka will use AI to understand the most important person in her business: her customer.
When you know exactly who you are selling to, selling becomes much easier.
Many business owners say, my product is for everybody.
But when you talk to everybody, nobody feels you are talking to them.
Your best customer is one real person. Let's call her Tolu.
Tolu has an age, a location, a job, and a budget.
She has a problem you solve, and a reason she hesitates before buying.
Let's write a customer profile. It answers six questions.
How old are they? Where do they live?
What work do they do? What can they spend?
What problem does your product solve for them? And what makes them hesitate?
With AI's help, you can write this in five minutes.
Here is a powerful trick. Copy your last twenty customer messages from WhatsApp or Instagram.
Remove names and phone numbers first. Keep your customers' details private.
Paste the messages into ChatGPT or Claude.
Then ask: what patterns do you see in who buys from me, and why?
AI will spot things you have been too busy to notice.
Next, ask AI to list the top ten questions and objections this customer might have.
Objections are the reasons people don't buy. It's too expensive. Will it fit me? Can I trust this seller?
When you know them, you can answer them before the customer even asks.
Now, where do you find more people like Tolu?
Ask AI: where does this customer spend time online? Which apps, groups, hashtags and events?
You might discover Facebook groups and Instagram hashtags full of your customers,
or church and school events, and markets you never thought of.
Two more ideas. First, turn every objection into a post that answers it.
If people ask about delivery, post a short video of an order being delivered.
Second, ask AI for ten partnership ideas with businesses that serve the same customer.
For example, a bridal boutique and a make-up artist can share customers and recommend each other.
Your assignment: write a one-page profile of your ideal customer, using AI.
Then edit it with what you know from real life, and include their top five questions or objections.
Submit it here in the academy, under Assignments.
In lesson three, we will use this profile to write adverts that sell. See you there!
3: Welcome back! In lesson two, Amaka got to know Tolu, her ideal customer.
Today, she will use AI to write the words that make Tolu want to buy.
Most good adverts follow a simple formula: Problem, Promise, Proof, Push.
Problem. Name the pain. No time to shop for work clothes?
Promise. Say what changes. Office-ready outfits at your door in twenty-four hours.
Proof. Give a reason to believe you, like reviews or numbers.
Push. End with one clear next step. Send STYLE on WhatsApp to order.
Now let AI do the first drafts. Ask for five captions using the formula, for your customer.
In seconds, you have five different adverts to choose from.
You can also ask AI to make a caption shorter, warmer, or end with a call to action.
Want it to sound like you? Paste three of your best past posts.
Then ask: write in this same voice.
Now the adverts sound like your brand, not like a robot.
Always edit what AI gives you. Add three real things.
A real customer quote,
a local detail, like where you deliver,
and a real price. That is what makes people trust you.
Your assignment: pick one product and write five adverts using Problem, Promise, Proof, Push.
Edit each one with a quote, a place and a price, then submit them under Assignments.
In lesson four, we will use AI to reply to customers fast. See you there!
4: Here is a simple truth. Customers who wait more than an hour for a reply often buy somewhere else.
With AI, Chidi replies in two minutes, clearly and kindly, even on a busy day. And the sale is made.
Build a reply bank. Ask AI to draft replies to your fifteen most common questions.
Price, delivery time, sizes, payment methods, and returns.
Save them as WhatsApp Business quick replies. Type a short word, tap, and the full answer is sent.
Ask AI for three polite replies that explain the value, without cutting your price.
Pick the one that sounds like you. Very often, the customer says yes.
When a customer is upset, paste their message into AI and ask for a calm, apologetic reply that offers a solution.
Say sorry, give a clear time, and offer something kind. That turns a problem into a loyal customer.
You can go even further. An AI sales agent answers on WhatsApp automatically, even at two in the morning.
It takes the order and sends a payment link, so the customer pays straight away.
JTR builds these sales agents for businesses like yours.
This week, build your reply bank, save your quick replies, and prepare one calm reply for upset customers.
In lesson five, we will follow up and close more sales. See you there!
5: Many customers say, I'll get back to you. And then they don't.
A friendly follow-up one day later,
and a last, gentle one after seven days, recovers many of these sales.
Ask AI to write a three-message follow-up sequence that gets gentler each time.
Now you never have to think about what to say. Just copy, adjust and send.
Keep a simple list of every lead: their name, the date, and what they asked about. A spreadsheet works well.
Each day, check who needs a follow-up, so nobody is forgotten.
When you talk about price, lead with the value first. What they get, and why it lasts.
Then offer options: a basic, a standard and a premium package. Most people choose the middle one.
Want to get better at price talks? Ask AI to play a customer who haggles.
Reply as you would in real life.
AI tells you how you did. Practise until it feels easy.
Send one clear payment link, and a clear delivery time.
After they pay, send a thank-you message and ask for a review.
Every review helps you win the next customer.
This week, start your lead list, write your follow-up sequence, make your three options, and practise with AI.
In lesson six, you will put it all together in your AI sales plan. See you there!
6: Welcome to the final lesson! Now you put everything together into a thirty-day AI sales plan for your own business.
It has five parts: your customer profile, twelve adverts or posts written with AI and edited by you, your reply bank for the top ten questions, your follow-up sequence, and one number you will track.
Spread the work over thirty days, so it is easy to keep up.
Schedule your twelve posts, about three each week.
And set your follow-up days, so no lead is forgotten.
Pick one number to track, for example enquiries per week, or sales per week.
Check it every week. When the number grows, you know your plan is working.
Put your plan in a Google Doc, a PDF or slides, with all five parts.
